Formulation
- Predisposing factors: Past medical history includes premature ovarian failure and prior HRT use (relevance to current vestibular symptoms not documented).
- Precipitating factors: Acute onset of continuous spinning vertigo and nausea while making breakfast earlier that morning (approximately two hours prior).
- Perpetuating factors: Prior similar episode about one month ago (short-lived then); ongoing symptoms without resolution at time of consult.
- Protective factors: Patient sought medical care, accepted prescription and plan to see GP; spouse present at home (reported).

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Provisional labyrinthitis / acute vertigo
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Obtain symptom relief (reduce spinning sensation, nausea)
  - Be able to ambulate safely and resume daily activities
  - Attend follow-up examination with GP/clinician
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Provide symptomatic relief to improve balance and reduce nausea
  - Perform ear/neurological examination and blood pressure measurement to exclude other causes
  - Escalate care to emergency department if red-flag symptoms develop
- Actions (Patient):
  - Take prescribed medication as directed: one tablet three times a day for ~10 days (medication name not documented; dose/route not documented)
  - Contact support/clinic to book GP appointment for ear examination and further assessment (patient stated intent to book)
  - Seek immediate emergency care (A&E) if new focal weakness (arms/legs), sudden severe headache, or violent vomiting occurs
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Prescribe symptomatic medication and send prescription to Lloyd Pharmacy (completed by clinician per transcript)
  - Arrange or ensure GP/clinic appointment in next few days for ear examination, blood pressure, gait and neurological assessment
  - Advise patient about emergency red flags and when to attend A&E

Secondary Problem: Nausea and ear buzzing/tinnitus with unsteadiness
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Reduce nausea and ear discomfort
  - Improve stability when walking
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Provide symptomatic antiemetic/vestibular-stabilizing treatment (as prescribed)
  - Monitor response to treatment and reassess if symptoms persist or worsen
- Actions (Patient):
  - Take prescribed medication as advised; rest as needed; avoid activities that increase fall risk until symptoms improve
  - Report lack of improvement or worsening symptoms at GP appointment or earlier if needed
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Review medication effectiveness at follow-up appointment
  - Perform otoscopic and neurological examination; consider further investigations or ENT referral if indicated

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered:
  - Explanation of provisional diagnosis "labyrinthitis" and its mechanism (inner ear inflammation/imbalance)
  - Rationale for symptomatic medication to improve stability
  - Need for GP examination (ear inspection, blood pressure, gait/neuro exam)
  - Clear red-flag signs to go to A&E: new limb weakness, sudden severe headache, violent vomiting
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening:
  - New or worsening limb weakness; sudden severe headache; violent vomiting; marked deterioration in balance or consciousness
- Coping Strategies:
  - Rest, avoid driving/operating machinery while symptomatic, take prescribed medication, arrange timely GP review, seek emergency care if red flags occur
